newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Tibet's Dalai Lama meets Taiwan VP Lien.
newsitem.headline: Tibet's Dalai Lama meets Taiwan VP Lien.

text.p: Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, met Taiwan Vice President Lien Chan on Wednesday for a private dinner, a Reuters correspondent who witnessed their arrival reported.

The unofficial, closed-door supper at a downtown Taipei hotel was a prelude to a controversial planned meeting on Thursday between the Dalai Lama and President Lee Teng-hui. Both meetings were certain to anger communist China.

Lee's aides on Wednesday gave the first official confirmation that the president would meet the Tibetan Buddhist god-king on the final day of his unprecedented six-day stay in Nationalist-ruled Taiwan.

The meeting with Lien, who doubles as premier or cabinet chief, was likely to pique China as it was arranged by the World League for Freedom and Democracy, a private group whose title once included the word "Anti-Communist".
Beijing already has assailed the Dalai Lama's planned meeting with Lee as the collusion of two "splittists" bent on severing both Tibet and Taiwan from the communist mainland.
The Dalai Lama arrived in Taiwan on Saturday, his first return to Chinese soil since he fled his Himalayan homeland in 1959 after an abortive uprising against Chinese rule.

The Dalai Lama and Taiwan's leaders deny that they seek independence from China. The Tibetan leader has said he wants only self-rule for Tibet, while Lee insists that Beijing first embrace democracy before Taiwan can reunite with the mainland.
